question: What primary type of data does a physical examination provide for the nurse?
explanation: Physical examinations rely on measurable and observable findings, which constitute objective clinical data. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Baseline health data obtained during an initial physical exam is primarily used for what purpose?
explanation: Baseline measurements give the nurse a starting point to monitor improvement or deterioration in a patient's condition. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is proper room lighting critical during a physical examination?

options.A: To observe subtle skin color changes accurately
options.B: To prevent the nurse from dropping medical tools
options.C: To reduce the overall temperature of the room
options.D: To keep the patient awake during the procedure

explanation: Good lighting allows the clinician to detect fine details like jaundice, cyanosis, or rashes on the skin. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: A nurse is about to examine a patient in a busy ward. What is the immediate first action to ensure a proper environment?

options.A: Ask all family members to leave the hospital
options.B: Turn off all overhead lighting in the room
options.D: Draw bedside curtains to secure patient privacy

explanation: Securing privacy protects patient dignity and establishes a safe environment before any physical assessment begins. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the single most effective way to prevent the spread of microorganisms in clinical settings?
explanation: Regular and proper hand hygiene drastically reduces the transmission of pathogens between patients and staff. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: When must a nurse apply standard infection control precautions?

options.A: When working in surgical units only
options.B: Only when caring for patients with known infections

explanation: Standard precautions apply universally to all patients to protect against unknown or unexpected pathogen exposures. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which assessment technique involves using the sense of touch to evaluate body tissues?
explanation: Palpation uses hands and fingers to feel for masses, tenderness, skin temperature, and moisture. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is auscultation performed before palpation during an abdominal physical examination?

options.A: To prevent altering normal bowel sounds
options.B: To complete the assessment more quickly
options.C: To make the patient feel more relaxed
options.D: To warm up the stethoscope diaphragm

explanation: Touching or pressing the abdomen early can stimulate peristalsis, falsely changing the frequency and character of bowel sounds. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h4)

question: When does the general survey of a patient officially begin?

options.A: After finishing the systemic physical examination
options.B: During the formal review of medical history
options.C: When measuring the patient's blood pressure
options.D: The moment the nurse first meets the patient

explanation: Observation of appearance, posture, and behavior starts immediately upon initial visual contact. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary clinical significance of abnormal vital signs in a patient?

options.A: They confirm the exact diagnosis of a viral infection
options.B: They indicate that the patient is ready for discharge
options.C: They replace the need for a comprehensive health history
options.D: They often serve as early warnings of clinical deterioration

explanation: Shifts in vital parameters frequently flag underlying physiological instability before other symptoms become obvious. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: What primary focus guides a respiratory system physical examination?

options.A: Pupillary reflex and cranial nerve function
options.B: Joint range of motion and muscle strength

explanation: Respiratory exams evaluate lung ventilation and airflow through visual inspection of the chest and auscultation of breath sounds. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: A patient reports left-sided chest pain. Which body system requires the most immediate and thorough physical examination?
explanation: Chest pain is a classic indicator of potential cardiac distress, making the cardiovascular system the top priority for evaluation. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h6)

question: How should physical examination findings be recorded in the patient record?

options.A: At the end of the work week to save time
options.B: Using general opinions and subjective impressions
options.D: Promptly and objectively with specific details

explanation: Documentation must rely on clear, factual, and measurable observations rather than vague or biased statements. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is accurate and timely documentation of assessment findings essential for patient care?

options.A: It facilitates safe communication among the healthcare team
options.B: It prevents patients from asking questions about treatment
options.C: It eliminates the need for any further nursing assessments
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will recover quickly

explanation: Clear written records allow doctors, nurses, and other providers to track changes and provide safe, continuous care. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)
